page_title: Two open source projects with great documentation

sources.entry: Two open source projects with great documentation (esbuild and redis)

summary.title: Two open source projects with great documentation
summary.one_liner: You learn what makes esbuild's and Redis's documentation (READMEs, architecture docs, changelogs, code comments) effective for helping newcomers understand design, structure, and decisions.
takeaways: A README should orient readers quickly: link to deeper docs and keep the first screen focused on the intended audience.
Architecture docs that state design principles first let readers infer the reasons behind later design choices.
Diagrams, graphs, and code snippets help explain looping or parallel processes that are hard to describe in text alone.
Detailed changelog entries with examples let readers understand a change's impact without reading the code diff.
Code comments should explain why, not restate trivial lines; comment non-obvious assertions and intent.
summary.summary: The author examines two open source projects, esbuild (a JavaScript bundler) and Redis (an in-memory database), as case studies of strong documentation. For each, he walks through the README, architecture documents, changelog or code comments, and explains why each piece helps newcomers understand where things are, how they work, and why they were built that way. He closes by arguing that documentation saves time for teams and maintainers, and that it is reasonable to skip documentation only for throwaway or personal projects.
